Actinic Keratoses (akiec).description: A precancerous scaly patch caused by long-term sun damage that can evolve into squamous cell carcinoma if untreated.
Actinic Keratoses (akiec).treatment: Cryotherapy, photodynamic therapy, or topical medications (e.g., 5-FU or imiquimod).
Actinic Keratoses (akiec).precautions: Avoid direct sunlight, use broad-spectrum sunscreen, and monitor skin changes.

severity_logic.mild: Single, small lesion with minimal scaling.
severity_logic.moderate: Multiple lesions or one with thicker scaling and redness.
severity_logic.severe: Widespread lesions with crusting or signs of bleeding; possible carcinoma development.

Actinic Keratoses (akiec).recommendation: Dermatologist evaluation recommended to prevent cancer progression.

Basal Cell Carcinoma (bcc).description: A slow-growing type of skin cancer that arises from the basal cells, often appearing as a shiny bump or open sore.
Basal Cell Carcinoma (bcc).treatment: Surgical excision, Mohs surgery, cryotherapy, or topical chemotherapy.
Basal Cell Carcinoma (bcc).precautions: Use sunscreen daily, avoid tanning beds, and perform regular skin checks.

severity_logic.mild: Small, well-defined lesion with no ulceration.
severity_logic.severe: Large, bleeding, or invasive lesion; potential tissue damage.

Basal Cell Carcinoma (bcc).recommendation: Consult a dermatologist for prompt treatment and removal.

Benign Keratosis (bkl).description: A non-cancerous, wart-like growth common in older adults, often brown or black in color.
Benign Keratosis (bkl).treatment: Generally none; cryotherapy or laser removal if bothersome.
Benign Keratosis (bkl).precautions: Avoid scratching or picking at lesions.

severity_logic.mild: Single small lesion with even color and surface.
severity_logic.moderate: Multiple or thick lesions with irritation or scaling.
severity_logic.severe: Rapidly growing, inflamed, or bleeding lesion (needs evaluation).

Benign Keratosis (bkl).recommendation: Benign; seek medical advice if lesion changes in color or shape.

Dermatofibroma (df).description: A harmless skin nodule caused by minor trauma or insect bites; firm to touch and slightly pigmented.
Dermatofibroma (df).treatment: No treatment required; surgical removal optional for cosmetic reasons.
Dermatofibroma (df).precautions: Avoid scratching or trauma to prevent inflammation.

severity_logic.mild: Small, stable lesion with no pain or redness.
severity_logic.moderate: Enlarged or irritated lesion due to friction.
severity_logic.severe: Painful, bleeding, or rapidly growing lesion.

Dermatofibroma (df).recommendation: Consult a dermatologist if lesion grows or becomes symptomatic.

Melanoma (mel).description: A highly dangerous form of skin cancer originating in melanocytes, often showing irregular color, shape, and border.
Melanoma (mel).treatment: Surgical removal, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, or radiation depending on stage.
Melanoma (mel).precautions: Use sunscreen daily, avoid tanning, and monitor moles monthly.

severity_logic.mild: Small, symmetrical mole with minimal irregularity.
severity_logic.moderate: Asymmetrical, multi-colored lesion with mild growth.
severity_logic.severe: Large, ulcerated, or bleeding lesion — possible metastasis.

Melanocytic Nevus (nv).description: A benign cluster of melanocytes that appears as a uniform, round, and small mole.
Melanocytic Nevus (nv).treatment: None unless atypical; surgical removal if irregular.
Melanocytic Nevus (nv).precautions: Monitor for changes using the ABCDE rule (Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter, Evolving).

severity_logic.mild: Stable, symmetric mole with no growth.
severity_logic.severe: Rapidly changing or irregular mole — may indicate malignancy.

Melanocytic Nevus (nv).recommendation: Monitor regularly; seek evaluation if the mole changes.

Vascular Lesion (vasc).description: Lesions formed by clusters of blood vessels that appear red, purple, or blue and may bleed easily.
Vascular Lesion (vasc).treatment: Laser therapy, cryotherapy, or surgical removal if symptomatic.
Vascular Lesion (vasc).precautions: Avoid trauma to prevent bleeding or irritation.

severity_logic.moderate: Raised lesion with mild irritation or occasional bleeding.
severity_logic.severe: Large, frequently bleeding or painful lesion.

Vascular Lesion (vasc).recommendation: Consult a dermatologist if bleeding or size increases.
